findings.title: 'Few left' slots are pulled out of the Morning and Afternoon groups into an unlabelled block above them
findings.description: On / (default, date-chosen, slot-chosen) slots with few places are shown first as an unlabelled block (08:20, 08:40, 09:00, 09:40, 10:20 ... 16:40), and the Morning and Afternoon groups below list only the remaining times. Saturday's Morning group reads 08:00, 09:20, 10:00, 11:00 ... and skips 08:20-09:40. The amber tags are also the loudest colour on the page.
findings.impact: A resident who wants 'Saturday morning' may scan the Morning row, conclude few early slots exist, and pick a later one or another day.

harm.statement: Residents booking for a clear-out who read the Morning group as the complete list of morning slots may miss free early slots (08:20-09:40) that sit in the unlabelled block above, and book a worse time or day.

evidence.detail: unlabelled Few-left block above Morning; Morning lacks 08:20-09:40

findings.recommendation: Decide whether scarcity or time organises the grid; if time, keep every slot in its period and let the availability tag mark scarcity in place.

findings.title: Cancelled booking is still headed 'Booked' and still promises a reminder
findings.description: done.html?status=cancelled keeps the H1 'Booked' and the full reference card; the cancellation is one bold red line under the reference, followed by unchanged copy 'Show this at the gate...' and 'A reminder will be sent to your mobile the evening before.'
findings.impact: The largest text on the page states the opposite of the booking's state.

harm.statement: A resident whose booking was cancelled may read 'Booked' and the large reference, drive to Quarry Road and be turned away at the gate because the booking is not on the gate's list.

evidence.detail: H1 Booked + red status line + unchanged gate/reminder copy

findings.recommendation: Let the cancelled state own the heading and the reference treatment, and drop instructions that apply only to a live booking.

findings.title: Expired-hold state shows the lost slot as a bare dash
findings.description: confirm.html with hold=expired: the error summary says 'This slot is no longer available.' and the summary row reads 'Slot – · Change slot'. The page does not say which time was lost, and 'Book this slot' remains the primary action below the filled fields.
findings.impact: The resident loses the reference point of which time they held; the primary button still invites booking a slot that is gone.

harm.statement: A resident whose 09:20 hold expired must go back to the grid without being told which time they lost, and may press 'Book this slot' first, slowing re-booking.

evidence.detail: Slot – · Change slot under the red summary

findings.recommendation: Decide what the expired state leads with: the lost time and the one way forward.

findings.title: Permit number field shown when no van or trailer is chosen
findings.description: On vehicle.html in the errors and info-open states (no vehicle chosen) the 'Permit number' label, hint and input appear under the vehicle chips; the label sits tight against the chip row.
findings.impact: Car drivers may think a permit is needed for every booking.

harm.statement: Residents booking a car, who do not know the permit rule, may think they also need a DRC- permit and stop to look for one.

evidence.detail: permit field with no vehicle selected

findings.recommendation: Decide whether the permit field belongs to the van/trailer choice only.

findings.title: Identity is only the council name in bold body text
findings.description: Every route opens with a stock bin glyph and 'Dunmore District Council' at body size; nothing names the recycling centre or Quarry Road until the footer, and nothing from the centre's own world (its waste streams, its gate, its signage) carries the page.
findings.impact: The service reads as a generic council form; DESIGN.md asks for 'plain, not bare'. Design note, no user harm claimed.
findings.recommendation: Decide which element of the centre's own world should carry identity on every step, within the Restrained strategy.

findings.title: Reference on the done page is not set as something to show at the gate
findings.description: DR-204117 is a ~32px bold line inside a full-width white card whose text stops at ~720px; the card leaves a large empty right half at 1280, and an empty pale band sits under the footer.
findings.impact: The one thing residents carry to the gate has no presence as a pass; the page looks unfinished at wide widths. Design note, no user harm claimed.

evidence.detail: reference card, half-width second card, band under footer

findings.recommendation: Decide how the reference should read when held up on a phone at the gate, and make that the done page's focal point.

findings.title: Card widths do not match their content at wide widths
findings.description: At 1280/1440 the 'Opening days', 'Your booking' and 'Your reference' cards span 1088px while their text runs to ~620-720px; forms and the 'At the centre' card are ~610px. Columns stop short and cards stand half empty.
findings.impact: Pages look unfinished on desktop; there is no single column edge to follow. Design note, no user harm claimed.
findings.recommendation: Decide one content width per step and hold cards to it.

strengths: Gate-attendant copy states rules where they apply (rubble and mattress limits, DRC- hint, 'not on the gate's list').
One filled button per step and a composed dark theme with lightened greens.
Slot tiles make Full vs free legible at a glance in both themes.
keep: Keep the plain, rule-beside-the-control voice and the one-primary-per-step discipline.
not_assessable: Motion (120 ms fades) and hover/focus states cannot be judged from stills; no baseline, so pairwise was not run (DES-05 not_applicable).
